papers.title: Reporting of Pericardial Adverse Events with Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors: A Disproportionality Analysis of the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System
papers.abstract: Background. Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) can cause immune-related adverse events in almost any organ. While myocarditis has received the most attention, data on pericardial disease with ICI use are limited. We examined pericardial adverse event reporting with nine ICIs using the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS). Methods. We combined legacy AERS and current FAERS quarterly files from January 2011 to June 2026 into 18,629,240 unique cases, deduplicated by case number, and removed cases the FDA had listed as deleted. ICI exposure was identified from generic names, brand names, development code names and the active-ingredient field. Pericardial events were defined by seven MedDRA preferred terms. We estimated reporting odds ratios (ROR), proportional reporting ratios (PRR), Bayesian information components (IC) and empirical Bayes geometric means (EBGM). We also examined myocarditis co-reporting, time trends, a comparison with other antineoplastic agents, a MedDRA query-based outcome, and 14 alternative definitions. Results. The analysis included 18,514,045 cases: 277,434 involved an ICI, 34,792 carried a pericardial term, and 1,680 had both. Pericardial events were reported disproportionately with ICIs (ROR 3.35 (95% CI 3.19 to 3.52); PRR 3.34; IC025 1.62). Eight of nine agents had a ROR above 1 (3.32 to 5.63). Among the most frequently reported terms, estimates were highest for cardiac tamponade (5.59 (95% CI 4.98 to 6.28)), followed by pericardial effusion (3.83 (95% CI 3.60 to 4.07)) and pericarditis (2.09 (95% CI 1.89 to 2.31)). After removing cases that also reported myocarditis, the ROR was 3.13 (95% CI 2.98 to 3.30). Most sensitivity analyses gave similar estimates (ROR 3.13 to 3.47); defining exposure by generic drug names alone, which identified only 44% of exposed cases, gave 3.99. Compared with cases naming other L01 antineoplastic agents, the ROR was 1.13 (95% CI 1.08 to 1.19): 1.28 (95% CI 1.20 to 1.36) for ICI-only cases and 0.96 (95% CI 0.89 to 1.04) when another antineoplastic was also named. The ICI-specific reporting odds ratio fell each quarter (odds ratio 0.977 per quarter, 95% CI 0.973 to 0.980). Conclusions. In FAERS, pericardial events were reported more often with ICIs than with other drugs across most agents and terms; however, incidence and causation cannot be determined. The excess over other antineoplastic agents was small, and reporting disproportionality declined over time. These findings support clinical awareness of pericardial disease in patients receiving ICIs and warrant study in data that can measure incidence.

papers.title: Plantar Thermography for Longitudinal Remote Monitoring of Chronic Heart Failure
papers.abstract: Rural patients with heart failure (HF) have poor access to care, worse outcomes, and may benefit from at-home monitoring. We evaluated whether foot temperature measured using a thermographic floor mat was associated with invasively measured cardiac output and whether longitudinal temperature changes preceded HF events. We conducted a two-part prospective, observational single-center study using the SmartMat (Podimetrics, Somerville, MA), which acquires plantar thermograms and ambient temperature. In the acute study, patients undergoing clinically indicated right heart catheterization completed 4 scans on the same day. In the chronic study, patients with a HF hospitalization in the past year and New York Heart Association Class II-III symptoms were instructed to use the device and a scale daily for 6 months. A HF event was defined as receiving at least one dose of intravenous or subcutaneous diuretic. Thirty patients were enrolled in the acute study. Mean right hallux temperature positively correlated with thermodilution cardiac output (r=0.63, p<0.001). 42 patients were enrolled in the chronic study. Among patients experiencing an HF event, ambient-adjusted hallux temperature declined in the 15 days immediately preceding the event compared with days 15-30 before the event. Plantar thermograms are associated with invasively measured cardiac output and may detect subclinical worsening before HF events. Foot temperature may provide complementary information regarding HF decompensation, supporting further evaluation of plantar thermography for remote HF monitoring.

papers.title: Fully Automated Multi-Chamber Strain Profiling in Consecutive Patients Undergoing Transthoracic Echocardiography: Feasibility, Functional Clustering, and Prognostic Implications
papers.abstract: Aims: Myocardial strain enables sensitive assessment of cardiac function, but its clinical application has largely focused on individual chambers or selected patient populations. We evaluated the feasibility and clinical relevance of fully automated multi-chamber strain assessment in consecutive patients undergoing routine transthoracic echocardiography (TTE). Methods and results: This retrospective study included 8,350 consecutive adults undergoing TTE. A hospital-wide artificial intelligence (AI)-based system automatically measured left ventricular (LV) global longitudinal strain (LVGLS), left atrial (LA) reservoir strain (LASr), and right ventricular (RV) free-wall strain (RVFWS). AI-derived LVGLS was available from at least one apical view in 97.1% of patients and from all three views in 94.8%; LASr and RVFWS were available in 94.1% and 94.5%, respectively, resulting in complete multi-chamber strain assessment in 90.3%. Strain measures showed modest correlations with conventional chamber-specific echocardiographic parameters and differential associations with clinical outcomes. Gaussian mixture modeling identified three distinct clusters characterized by preserved multi-chamber function, RV-dominant dysfunction, and pan-chamber dysfunction. Compared with the preserved cluster, pan-chamber dysfunction was associated with the highest risk of all-cause death or heart failure hospitalization (adjusted hazard ratio, 3.44; 95% CI, 2.43-4.88; P<0.001). Prognostic associations remained evident in patients with LV ejection fraction (LVEF) [≥]50%, and cluster assignment provided incremental prognostic information beyond clinical factors, LVEF, and RV fractional area change. Conclusions: Fully automated multi-chamber strain assessment was feasible in a large consecutive TTE cohort. Integrating strain across cardiac chambers may provide complementary functional characterization and identify clinically relevant clusters with prognostic information beyond conventional assessment.

papers.title: Cardiac MRI at 3.0T in the presence of implantable cardioverter defibrillators (ICDs)
papers.abstract: Patients with implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs) often are excluded from receiving CMR scans at 3.0T due to ICD-induced image artifacts. This work aims to transfer sequence protocols established for CMR imaging in the presence of ICDs at 1.5T to a first human application at 3.0T. All measurements were performed on a clinical 3T MRI scanner. Phantom measurements were used to establish and optimize wideband PSIR LGE imaging at 3.0T. Volunteer measurements with externally placed ICDs were used for optimization of CINE imaging and wideband PSIR imaging. Thirdly, patients with implanted ICD were examined with the optimized protocols. Human measurements showed that SA stacks obtained with spoiled GRE after contrast agent showed a markedly lower artifact burden than the conventional approach. For scar imaging, a wideband PSIR with a bandwidth of 3kHz and a frequency offset of +750Hz allowed a sufficient suppression of relevant artifacts in the majority of scans. No strong correlation between the image quality and the distance between the cardiac silhouette and the device was detected. The presented work shows the feasibility of clinical cardiac MRI at 3.0T including GRE-CINE and wideband PSIR-LGE for patients with ICDs.

papers.title: Left Ventricular Diastolic Intraventricular Pressure Differences and Propagation Velocity with 4D-Flow MRI in Patients with Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
papers.abstract: Background: Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) remains the gold standard for assessing left ventricular (LV) diastolic dysfunction (DD), but noninvasive alternatives are needed to overcome geometric and acoustic limitations. 4D-Flow MRI enables comprehensive assessment of intraventricular pressure differences (IVPDs) and flow propagation velocity (VP). We aimed to evaluate 4D-Flow-derived IVPDs and VP in patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM). Methods: Thirty-eight HCM patients and 38 age- and sex-matched healthy controls underwent TTE and 4D-Flow MRI. Spatiotemporal maps of velocity and IVPDs, decomposed into inertial and convective components, were derived along the main inflow streamline from the mitral valve to the apex. Peak early filling rate (PEFR) was used to normalize IVPDs and VP. Results: While absolute peak flow rates were comparable, HCM patients exhibited significantly faster VP (100.4 vs. 60.2 cm/s, p < 0.01) and higher positive early E IVPD (1.40 vs. 0.92 mmHg, p < 0.01) compared to controls. Normalizing IVPDs by PEFR amplified group differences, revealing a markedly increased flow-normalized E-IVPD (5.13 vs. 2.94 x 103 mmHg.ml1.s, p < 0.001) and deeper reverse ER IVPD (-6.06 vs. -4.61 x 103 mmHg.ml1.s, p < 0.01) in HCM. These differences were primarily driven by the inertial components. Multivariable analysis demonstrated that ER IVPD is independently determined by PEFR and the TTE E/E' ratio (r = 0.65, p < 0.001). Conclusions: 4D-Flow MRI-derived, flow-normalized IVPDs and propagation velocity provide robust, noninvasive markers of altered LV chamber stiffness and impaired diastolic filling in HCM, offering deeper 3D hemodynamic insights into diastolic dysfunction.

papers.title: Prevalence and Clinical Correlates of Coronary Perivascular Inflammation in an Asymptomatic Adult Primary Prevention Population: An Assessment of the CT-Derived Fat Attenuation Index Score (FAI-Score)
papers.abstract: Background: Coronary perivascular fat attenuation index score (FAI-Score) on coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) quantifies vascular inflammation and predicts cardiac mortality in symptomatic cohorts. However, its prevalence, anatomical distribution, and clinical correlates in asymptomatic primary prevention populations remain uncharacterized. Methods: In an IRB-approved prospective study across two clinical sites, 84 consecutive asymptomatic adults (mean age 53.7 {+/-} 8.6 years; 63.1% men) with no prior coronary artery disease underwent screening CCTA and comprehensive clinical, metabolic, and biomarker profiling. AI-standardized FAI-Score was quantified across three epicardial vessels (LAD, LCx, RCA). High and very high perivascular inflammation were pre-specified as any vessel [≥]75th and [≥]90th percentiles, respectively. Luminal stenosis and plaque were graded using CAD-RADS 2.0. Results: Elevated FAI-Score ([≥]75th percentile) was present in 42.9% of participants (36/84; 95% CI 32.8% - 53.5%), with 17.9% (15/84; 95% CI 11.1% - 27.4%) exhibiting very high inflammation ([≥]90th percentile). Multi-vessel inflammation was identified in 17.9% (15/84), with the RCA most frequently involved ([≥]90th percentile in 13.1%). Standard circulating biomarkers, including ApoB, non-HDL-C, HbA1c, and PREVENT-ASCVD 10-year risk showed no association with binary inflammation. Systemic hs-CRP (median 0.8 mg/L) exhibited an inverse correlation with maximum vessel FAI-Score (Spearman {rho}=-0.27, p=0.014). Men demonstrated higher rates of elevated FAI-Score than women (52.8% vs. 25.8%, p=0.016; [≥]90th percentile: 26.4% vs. 3.2%, p=0.007). Strikingly, 46.2% (30/65) of participants with normal luminal anatomy (CAD-RADS 0) and 47.2% (25/53) with zero plaque burden harbored elevated FAI-Score; all 15 individuals with very high FAI-Score had CAD-RADS 0 (Fisher's exact p=0.018). Body mass index was the sole secondary correlate surviving false discovery rate correction (AUC = 0.71, p=0.001, all-test FDR q=0.028). Regularized multivariable models showed modest out-of-sample discrimination for FAI-Score elevation (cross-validated AUC = 0.71). Conclusions: Coronary perivascular inflammation is common among asymptomatic adults and frequently uncouples from structural plaque and luminal stenosis. Routine circulating biomarkers and clinical risk calculators fail to identify inflamed vessels, highlighting FAI-Score as an independent dimension of primary cardiovascular risk assessment.

papers.title: Hidden in Plain Sight: Clinical Profile, Diagnosis, and Outcomes of Cardiac Amyloidosis in Cali, Colombia
papers.abstract: Background Cardiac amyloidosis is an increasingly recognized cause of heart failure in older adults, yet Colombian data, and data from the southwest of the country in particular, remain scarce. We describe the clinical, diagnostic, imaging and outcome profile of patients with cardiac amyloidosis at two high-complexity institutions in Cali. Methods Observational, descriptive, retrospective, two-center study. Patients were identified in the institutional registries of both centers using ICD-10 codes for amyloidosis, and clinical data were abstracted manually from medical records. Continuous variables are reported as median (interquartile range) and categorical variables as counts and percentages over the number of patients with available data. Results Thirty-two patients were analyzed (median age 77 years; 68.8% men). Heart failure (90.6%), atrial fibrillation (46.9%) and carpal tunnel syndrome (31.2%) were frequent. The etiological classification depended on the test considered: bone scintigraphy was positive (Perugini 2-3) in 23 of 26 patients studied (88.5%), but a monoclonal protein was screened for in only 22, and the full non-invasive criteria for ATTR were met in 16 of 32 (50.0%). Genetic testing was positive in 9 of 18 tested, and the variant was Val142Ile in all 8 patients in whom it was characterized. The working diagnosis was ATTR in 26 patients (81.2%) and AL in 6 (18.8%). Tafamidis was used in 37.5%. Eleven of the 31 patients with known vital status died (35.5%), and NT-proBNP was markedly higher among those who died (6640 vs 1186 pg/mL; p=0.003). Conclusions In this southwestern Colombian cohort, cardiac amyloidosis presented as the classic transthyretin phenotype, with the Val142Ile variant in all 8 patients in whom it was characterized. Bone scintigraphy was frequently positive, but screening for a monoclonal protein was often omitted, so only half the cohort met the full non-invasive criteria for ATTR. Mortality was high and closely associated with NT-proBNP.

papers.title: Preoperative Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index and Clinical Outcomes After Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
papers.abstract: Background: The systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) is a routinely available blood-derived marker with potential prognostic relevance after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). We evaluated associations between preoperative SII and postoperative outcomes. Methods: PubMed, Embase, Scopus and Web of Science were searched to 1 October 2026, with supplementary searches through 14 October 2026. Peer-reviewed observational studies evaluating preoperative SII in adults undergoing CABG were eligible. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Compatible categorical associations and exploratory adjusted continuous mortality effects were pooled separately using restricted maximum-likelihood random-effects models; other findings were summarized descriptively. Results: Thirty-one reports were included, with an aggregate sample of 30,976 and possible cohort overlap; five contributed to meta-analysis. Two off-pump cohorts comprising 1,378 patients and 180 atrial-fibrillation events yielded an imprecise crude association with postoperative atrial fibrillation (OR 1.60, 95%CI 0.53-4.82; I2=68%). An exploratory crude synthesis indicated greater intra-aortic balloon pump use with higher SII (OR 2.45, 95%CI 1.16-5.18; I2=51%). Two cohorts with differing follow-up yielded an exploratory adjusted mortality HR of 1.11 (95% Wald CI 1.05-1.18) per study-specific SD increase in log-SII. In one 624-patient cohort, high SII was associated with postoperative acute kidney injury after adjustment (OR 3.35, 95% CI 2.25-4.97).Apparent atrial-fibrillation discrimination varied (AUC 0.587-0.946). Conclusions: Preoperative SII showed associations with selected adverse outcomes after CABG, supporting further evaluation as an accessible prognostic marker. Its incremental value beyond established clinical risk models requires validation. Keywords: Systemic immune-inflammation index; Coronary artery bypass grafting; Atrial fibrillation; Prognosis; Systematic review

papers.title: Teaching an ECG model where to look does not make it more robust to missing leads: a pre-registered comparison of guideline-based attention guidance with random lead masking
papers.abstract: Background. Real-world 12-lead electrocardiograms (ECGs) often have missing or corrupted leads. A deep-learning classifier can be prepared for this by random lead masking during training, or by injecting clinical knowledge, for example by pulling its attention towards the leads that guidelines use for each diagnosis. Whether this knowledge adds robustness beyond masking is unknown. Methods. Pre-registered comparison of three arms sharing one network (per-lead 1D-ResNet encoder and per-diagnosis attention over the 12 leads): standard training (M0); random whole-lead masking (M1); masking plus a Kullback-Leibler penalty pulling attention towards a fixed guideline-derived key-lead map (M2, guideline-based attention guidance). Six diagnoses; five seeds per arm. Development on PTB-XL (21,799 ECGs); single sealed evaluation on PTB-XL fold 10 (2,198 ECGs) and on CODE-15% (233,204 exams, external validation). Primary endpoint: AUROC difference M2 - M1, averaged over first-degree AV block, right and left bundle branch block and atrial fibrillation and over 1 to 6 lost (zeroed) leads, with a patient-level paired BCa bootstrap 95% confidence interval. Results. The guidance did not change robustness: {Delta}AUROC -0.0010 (95% CI -0.0033 to +0.0006), an interval entirely within the pre-specified +-0.02 margin; the result was unchanged with another bootstrap seed, other interval methods and leave-one-diagnosis-out analyses. Masking improved AUROC: M1 - M0 = +0.0134 (95% CI +0.0102 to +0.0172) when one key lead was lost, and the number of lost leads tolerated before AUROC fell by more than 0.02 rose from 7 (M0) to 10 (M1). M2 attention matched the map and M2 was non-inferior on intact ECGs, but its calibration slope was lower for all six diagnoses in both datasets. M2 lost slightly more when all key leads were lost together (-0.0067) and gained only when one to three leads remained (exploratory; AUROC 0.9408 vs 0.9210 with 11 leads lost). CODE-15% reproduced every pattern (primary -0.0007, 95% CI -0.0011 to -0.0003). Conclusions. Random lead masking suffices to make an ECG classifier robust to missing leads; adding guideline knowledge aligns attention with clinical criteria but adds no robustness and worsens calibration. Guideline-aligned attention should not be taken as evidence of robustness.

papers.title: Narrow Is Slow: CT-Derived Anatomic Isthmus 3 Width and Arrhythmogenic Substrate in Repaired Tetralogy of Fallot
papers.abstract: Background: Anatomic isthmus 3 (AI 3) is defined as the myocardium between the pulmonary valve annulus and the ventricular septal defect patch that persists after tetralogy of Fallot (ToF) repair. Ventricular tachycardia (VT) propagated through slow conducting AI 3 (SCAI 3) represents a significant cause of morbidity in ToF. There is an unmet need for non-invasive identification of SCAI 3 in patients with ToF. Objectives: To assess whether the anatomic features of AI 3 as derived from cardiac computed tomography (CT) can predict slow conduction velocity during EP study. Methods: This retrospective single-center study included patients with ToF who underwent an electrophysiologic study and had AI 3 width measured from the pre-procedure cardiac CT. All patients underwent programmed ventricular stimulation, and electroanatomic. Logistic regression was performed to assess the relationship between AI 3 width and the presence of SCAI 3. Results: Of 27 consecutive patients with ToF, twelve patients were found to have SCAI 3, and ten patients were found to have SCAI 3 mediated VT. The AI 3 was significantly narrower in patients with SCAI 3 compared to those with normal AI 3 conduction (18.4 +/- 6.6 mm vs. 29.2 +/- 9.0 mm; p = 0.001). An AI 3 width above 21.5 mm carried a negative predictive value of 80.0%. Conclusion: In adults with repaired ToF referred for electrophysiology study, a narrower CT-derived AI 3 width was associated with SCAI 3 identification. AI 3 width measured on a CT obtained before PV replacement could help guide invasive risk stratification.

papers.title: Deep learning-based electrocardiographic differentiation of Takotsubo syndrome from acute anterior myocardial infarction: explainability, human-AI interaction, and a utilization bias hypothesis
papers.abstract: BackgroundArtificial intelligence (AI) may improve electrocardiographic differentiation of Takotsubo syndrome from acute anterior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), but its impact on human diagnostic performance, the added value of visual explanations, and differences by reader background and experience remain uncertain. MethodsUsing 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) images from two hospitals, we developed and externally validated an ensemble of three deep learning models after self-supervised pretraining and fine-tuning. The diagnostic task used ECGs recorded within 14 days after symptom onset, regardless of reperfusion status. We conducted a four-phase reader study. Phases 1-3 compared unaided interpretation, a reference sheet, and additional AI assistance. In Phase 4, readers evaluated a new ECG set after randomization to reference-sheet support alone, with AI predictions, or with AI predictions plus gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) heatmaps. Diagnostic correctness was analyzed using generalized linear mixed-effects models. Exploratory analyses examined differences by cardiologist status and experience. ResultsDevelopment and external-validation cohorts, including healthy controls, comprised 832 and 95 participants, respectively. For Takotsubo-STEMI discrimination, external-validation accuracy was 0.914, with areas under the receiver operating characteristic and precision-recall curves of 0.970 and 0.984. Seventy healthcare providers completed the reader study. The estimated probability of correct diagnosis increased from 0.632 without assistance to 0.864 with AI assistance (odds ratio [OR], 3.71; P<0.001). In randomized Phase 4, AI assistance improved accuracy vs reference-sheet support alone (OR, 4.28; 95% CI, 3.08-5.95; P<0.001), and Grad-CAM provided additional benefit (OR, 1.53; 95% CI, 1.04-2.25; P=0.033). Exploratory analyses showed greater improvement among less experienced readers; with AI assistance, non-cardiologists outperformed cardiologists. AI-assisted readers remained less accurate overall than the model alone. ConclusionsAn ECG image-based ensemble differentiated Takotsubo syndrome from anterior STEMI and improved reader accuracy. Visual explanations provided additional benefit, while experience-related differences highlight the importance of effective human-AI interaction. Clinical PerspectiveO_ST_ABSWhat is new?C_ST_ABSO_LIAn electrocardiogram (ECG) image-based ensemble deep learning model differentiated Takotsubo syndrome from acute anterior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction with an external-validation accuracy of 0.914 and ROC AUC of 0.970 and exceeded mean reader accuracy on the reader-study ECG sets. C_LIO_LIIn a human diagnostic test, displaying the models prediction improved readers diagnostic performance, and adding gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) explanation produced further gains. C_LIO_LIExploratory analyses showed greater improvement and higher AI-assisted accuracy among less experienced readers, with reversal of cardiologists unaided advantage under AI assistance, motivating a utilization bias hypothesis. C_LI What Are the Clinical Implications?O_LIThe model exceeded mean unaided and AI-assisted reader accuracy on the reader-study ECG sets, supporting its potential to aid differentiation of Takotsubo syndrome from acute anterior myocardial infarction. C_LIO_LIAI assistance improved reader diagnostic accuracy, with further benefit from Grad-CAM visualizations, supporting further evaluation of these tools in clinical practice. C_LIO_LIConventional clinical expertise may not ensure effective AI use, warranting further studies to test the utilization bias hypothesis and determine whether training in integrating AI predictions can improve performance across reader backgrounds and experience levels. papers.title: Functional fine-mapping of the 9p21.3 cardiovascular disease locus implicates the lncRNA MIR31HG as an effector transcript in endothelial cells
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The chromosome 9p21.3 locus is among the strongest genetic risk loci for cardiovascular disease (CVD), yet the regulatory mechanisms underlying this association remain poorly understood. Previous vascular disease studies focused predominantly on the role of this locus in smooth muscle cell (SMC) dysfunction, whereas its potential role in endothelial cells (ECs) remains less well characterized. Here, we sought to identify candidate regulatory variants at 9p21.3, their distal target genes, and effector transcripts that contribute to CVD-related phenotypes in ECs. METHODS: Promoter capture Hi-C was used to map chromatin interactions at 9p21.3 in primary human ascending aortic SMCs (n=6), supplementing the previously obtained ECs (n=16) dataset. To support the regulatory relevance of these interactions, expression quantitative trait locus analysis was performed in 136 vascular biopsies. Variant effects were prioritized in silico using AlphaGenome. The regulatory activity of the prioritized region was validated using CRISPR activation. RESULTS: Chromatin interaction mapping identified a complex regulatory architecture at the 9p21.3 locus involving 19 putative regulatory elements and 15 genes across ECs and SMCs. MIR31HG showed the most recurrent distal promoter connectivity with the 9p21.3 region. Consistent with the chromatin interaction map, expression of MIR31HG transcripts was associated with genetic variation at the 9p21.3 locus. In ECs, the lncRNA MIR31HG, but not miR-31, was responsive to hemodynamic flow. Depletion of MIR31HG in ECs was associated with endothelial activation. Epigenetic tracks and deep learning predictions highlighted an active enhancer element at 9p21.3, which was subsequently validated by CRISPR activation and increased MIR31HG expression, confirming its capacity to regulate MIR31HG over a large genomic distance of approximately 538 kb. CONCLUSIONS: Altogether, these data implicate lncRNA MIR31HG as a likely effector of the 9p21.3 CVD locus, linking the cis-regulatory element and heritable genetic variation in the respective region to endothelial activation through long-range enhancer regulation.

papers.title: Heart rate variability and electrocardiographic parameters among workers exposed to chronic intermittent hypobaric hypoxia in the Peruvian Andes: A cross-sectional study Cardiac autonomic function in Andean workers
papers.abstract: Chronic intermittent hypobaric hypoxia is an occupational exposure experienced by workers who alternate between high-altitude worksites and lower-altitude resting locations. Its effects on cardiac autonomic modulation and electrocardiographic parameters remain insufficiently characterized in Andean workers. This study aimed to compare heart rate variability and electrocardiographic parameters between workers exposed to chronic intermittent hypobaric hypoxia and controls working permanently at lower altitude in Arequipa, Peru. An observational cross-sectional study was conducted in 96 male workers aged 20-60 years. The exposed group included 53 workers performing rotational shifts at altitudes [≥]3,000 m above sea level with rest periods at <2,500 m, while the control group included 43 workers working permanently at <2,500 m. Heart rate variability was assessed during the morning rest period in Arequipa, at approximately 2,300 m above sea level, using a Polar(R) H10 heart rate sensor after 15 minutes of rest. Participants also underwent standard 12-lead electrocardiography. Vital signs were clinically similar between groups. No statistically significant differences were observed in PR interval, corrected QT interval, time-domain heart rate variability parameters, or frequency-domain heart rate variability parameters. In this sample of apparently healthy male workers evaluated during their rest period at moderate altitude, exposure to chronic intermittent hypobaric hypoxia was not associated with significant differences in resting heart rate variability or standard electrocardiographic parameters.

papers.title: Pre-Deployment Cardiovascular Risk Assessment and Outcomes among United States Antarctic Program Participants: Insights from Contemporary Risk Models
papers.abstract: BackgroundCardiovascular (CV) screening is critical for personnel deploying to Antarctica, where geographic isolation and limited medical care make the management of acute cardiovascular events challenging. The utility of contemporary risk prediction tools such as the AHA PREVENT equations in this unique population remains uncertain. MethodsWe retrospectively analyzed 154 individuals referred for enhanced CV evaluation before deployment to the U.S. Antarctic Program (USAP). Participants were evaluated across three temporal cohorts (2018-2020, 2021-2023, and 2024-2026). Demographics, CV risk factors, cardiac testing, and deployment clearance outcomes were collected. Risk was estimated using the Framingham Risk Score (FRS), AHA/ACC Pooled Cohort Equations (PCE), and AHA PREVENT risk models. ResultsThe cohort was predominantly male (79.9%; mean age 44.6 {+/-} 14.6 years), and abnormal ECG was the most common referral trigger (70.8%). Median 10-year risk was low by PREVENT and FRS and borderline elevated by PCE (PREVENT 2.7% [IQR 1.1-6.6], FRS 2.3% [IQR 0.5-7.1], and PCE 6.1% [IQR 2.4-9.2]). Among 72 participants with all scores, 51% were classified discordantly; PREVENT ASCVD agreed closely with FRS ({kappa}=0.77) but poorly with PCE ({kappa}=0.24-0.35), which consistently estimated higher risk. PCE was calculable in 52.6% versus 70.8% for PREVENT. Overall, 132 participants (85.7%) were cleared for deployment, while 8 (5.2%) were not physically qualified (NPQ); 6 of these NPQs were due to cardiovascular causes. Of 22 cardiac medical evacuations during the study period, 21 involved individuals without prior advanced cardiovascular screening. One screened individual was evacuated for symptoms subsequently found to have no cardiac cause. ConclusionsRisk calculators disagree substantially in the fitness-selected population. We recommend PREVENT as the primary risk-stratification tool as it is the most contemporary derivation, incorporates renal function, is race-agnostic, extends to heart failure, applies from age 30, and agrees closely with FRS, easing transition. Targeted imaging, including coronary artery calcium scoring, may supplement intermediate-risk candidates.

papers.title: Results of a Community-Based Coronary CT Angiography Screening in Asymptomatic Adults With Cardiovascular Risk Factors: The Broward County Heart Project
papers.abstract: BackgroundCoronary CT angiography (CCTA) and calcium scoring detect subclinical coronary atherosclerosis, but the results of community-based screening in asymptomatic adults with cardiovascular risk factors are poorly described. ObjectiveTo describe the results of the first phase of a county-funded CT screening program and their variation by demographics, health system, time, and ZIP code. MethodsRetrospective analysis of aggregate reports from the Broward County Florida Heart Project (May 2023-September 2025). Eligible residents were those with insurance coverage, age 45-70 years (limited exceptions), free of known cardiovascular disease and symptoms, with at least one risk factor. Examinations at six hospitals in four health systems were classified by the program team as normal (Category 1), abnormal (Category 2), or very abnormal (Category 3), with a separate flag for other non-coronary abnormality. We used Wilson confidence intervals and chi-square, trend, and Mantel-Haenszel tests. ResultsAmong 7,135 participants (58.3% men; 79.0% White, 8.0% Black, 17.2% Hispanic), 43.2% had Category 1, 45.4% Category 2, and 11.4% Category 3 results; 56.8% (95% CI, 55.7%-58.0%) had abnormal or very abnormal results. The proportion rose from 39.3% at 45-55 years to 78.5% at 71 or older (trend P<0.001) and was higher in men than women (68.9% vs 39.8%; odds ratio [OR], 3.36; 95% CI, 3.05-3.71). Rates were lower in Black than White participants (38.9% vs 58.6%; hospital-adjusted OR, 0.45; 95% CI, 0.38-0.54) and in Hispanic than non-Hispanic participants (51.0% vs 57.8%). Abnormal results ranged from 39.5% to 60.3% across health systems (P<0.001). Variation across the 50 highest-volume ZIP codes did not exceed chance (P=0.53). ConclusionsMore than half of insured, asymptomatic adults with risk factors screened in this community program had abnormal results, with steep age and sex gradients and unexplained variation across health systems.

papers.title: Cardiomyocyte-Derived Cell-Free DNA in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
papers.abstract: IntroductionIn hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), wall stress and subclinical myocardial injury related in part to pathological hypercontractility, which in turn are associated with worse outcomes. Cell-free DNA (cfDNA) is released from cardiomyocytes (cfDNA-CM) through irreversible cellular injury and death. We investigated the feasibility of quantifying cfDNA-CM and its relationship to HCM patient characteristics. MethodsWe analyzed 57 plasma samples from stable patients with HCM and 10 plasma samples from patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Plasma cfDNA was isolated from both groups. Whole genome bisulfite sequencing (WGBS) libraries were generated and sequenced with short-read sequencing. Methylation patterns were used for tissue deconvolution analysis and cell-specific cfDNA quantification. ResultsYields of cfDNA (p = 0.003) and cfDNA-CM (p = 0.002) fractions were higher in AMI controls than HCM, supporting the validity of the assay. Within the HCM cohort, the median cfDNA yield was 12.22 ng [IQR: 7.77, 18.94]. The cfDNA-CM fraction in this cohort ranged from 0% to 6.4% of total cfDNA. Higher cfDNA-CM tertiles were associated with higher body mass index (BMI, p=0.001), a greater prevalence of BMI [≥]30 kg/m{superscript 2} (p<0.001), and a higher prevalence of obstructive sleep apnea (p=0.038). No significant differences were observed in other demographic, genetic, and laboratory characteristics. Higher cfDNA-CM tertile was numerically associated with higher New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class and left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction, while circulating biomarkers of wall stress (NT-proBNP) and myocardial injury (troponin) did not differ across tertiles (p=0.83 and p=0.29, respectively). ConclusionIsolation and quantification of cfDNA as well as detection of cfDNA-CM in chronic stable patients with HCM are feasible. Higher cfDNA-CM fraction was associated with increasing BMI and cardiometabolic comorbidity burden. The absence of association with traditional circulating biomarkers suggests that cfDNA-CM may reflect a distinct domain of myocardial health, injury, and adverse remodeling.

papers.title: Feasibility of continuous finger arterial pressure recording with synchronised facial video in a hypertension clinic cohort: the BP-WAVE pilot study
papers.abstract: IntroductionWhether the arterial pressure waveform carries structural vascular information beyond brachial pressure, and whether facial video can read its shape, are uncertain. We sought to determine whether continuous finger arterial pressure recording with synchronised facial video, linked to existing coronary calcium imaging, is feasible in a hypertension clinic, whether a consumer camera recovers heart rate and pulse shape, and the exploratory association between waveform morphology and coronary calcium. MethodsBP-WAVE is a single-site prospective observational pilot study. The primary outcome was feasibility: recruitment, consent, completeness of recording, imaging availability and data completeness. Secondary outcomes were waveform quality, device agreement, feature availability and video recovery of heart rate and pulse shape. Exploratory outcomes were Spearman correlations of 14 waveform features with the Agatston calcium score, with exact permutation p values adjusted within families. ResultsNine of ten planned participants were recorded over 12 days (median age 55 years, range 40 to 74; five women). Nine of 15 patients approached consented (60%, 95% CI 32.3 to 83.7%); all nine completed the recording with video and had a calcium score (median 351, range 33 to 1816). Of 4,178 detected beats, 2,965 (71%) passed quality control. Video recovered heart rate within 0.4 to 4.1 beats per minute in eight of nine participants, and camera pulse shape exceeded a phase-randomised benchmark in six of nine (held-out r 0.48 to 0.76). Form factor had the strongest correlation with calcium (rho -0.75, 95% CI -0.94 to -0.17, exact p 0.025, q 0.36); no association met the Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted significance threshold (126 tests in nine families; smallest q 0.14). ConclusionIn this imaging-selected pilot of nine hypertension clinic patients, continuous finger arterial pressure recording with synchronised facial video and linkage to coronary calcium was feasible, a consumer camera recovered heart rate in eight and its pulse shape exceeded a phase-randomised benchmark in six, and no waveform-calcium association met the multiple-testing-adjusted significance threshold.

papers.title: Foundation Model Artificial Intelligence for Electrocardiogram Detection of Rheumatic Mitral Stenosis
papers.abstract: BackgroundRheumatic mitral stenosis (RMS) disproportionately affects low-resource settings where echocardiography is limited. We evaluated foundation model (FM) feasibility for RMS detection using limited, indirectly labeled ECGs. MethodsAn ECG-FM was fine-tuned using 804 RMS-positive ECGs per fold and externally validated across clinical and wearable lead configurations. ResultsInternal AUROCs were 0.89, 0.87, and 0.87, for 12-Lead, 6-Lead, and 1-Lead respectively. External AUROCs were 0.82, 0.80, and 0.77. Performance remained comparable across demographic subgroups. ConclusionsFM fine-tuning enables RMS detection using limited ICD-derived labels, supporting further evaluation of reduced-lead ECG screening and echocardiography triage in resource-constrained settings.

papers.title: Blood Pressure and Heart Rate Stationarity in Predicting TEVAR Response
papers.abstract: BackgroundHypertension is a major risk factor for type B aortic dissections and rupture, with guidelines recommending systolic blood pressure (SBP) control below 130 mmHg to improve outcomes. While post-TEVAR blood pressure is often managed with a focus on mean SBP, little is known about temporal hemodynamic patterns and their association with surgical success. This study investigates blood pressure and heart rate (HR) time-series metrics within 24 hours post-TEVAR and their predictive potential for outcomes. MethodsBlood pressure (n = 560) and HR (n = 680) time-series data from 31 patients were analyzed alongside preoperative aortic geometry metrics. Exploratory data analysis identified correlations between BP variability and outcomes. Stationarity tests were performed on time-series data to assess statistical properties. Logistic regression models incorporating hemodynamic metrics, along with CT-derived features, were used to predict TEVAR outcomes. ResultsSuccessful outcomes correlated with greater diastolic blood pressure variability and strictly stationary SBP. Logistic regression models combining these metrics along with heart rate standard deviation and preoperative aortic geometry achieved 96.67% 5-fold cross-validation accuracy in predicting outcomes. ConclusionPost-TEVAR behaviors of hemodynamic variables are critical predictors of TEVAR success, with higher DBP standard deviation and strict stationarity of SBP significantly associated with favorable outcomes. These findings highlight the importance of hemodynamic variability and stationarity in optimizing post-TEVAR patient care.

papers.title: Temporal Trends and Demographic Disparities in Percutaneous Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion Utilization in the United States, 2016-2022
papers.abstract: BackgroundLeft atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) provides non-pharmacological stroke prevention for non-valvular atrial fibrillation patients with contraindications to long-term oral anticoagulation. National long-term data on age-adjusted utilization trends and demographic adoption disparities remain limited. ObjectivesTo evaluate national temporal trends, hospital characteristics, clinical acuity shifts, and demographic adoption patterns of percutaneous LAAO procedures. MethodsUsing the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) from 2016 through 2022, percutaneous LAAO procedures were identified using ICD-10-PCS code 02L73DK. Weighted national estimates were used to evaluate patient demographics, hospital factors, clinical acuity, and overall in-hospital mortality. Age-adjusted rates per 100,000 population were calculated using direct standardization to the 2000 U.S. standard population. ResultsA total of 190,020 weighted LAAO procedures were identified increasing from 4,875 in 2016 to 60,445 in 2022. The mean patient age was 76.3 {+/-} 7.6 years, and 58.5% were male. Most patients were White (90.4%), while Hispanic (4.3%), Black (3.9%), and Asian/Pacific Islander (1.3%) patients accounted for smaller proportions of procedures. Most procedures were performed at urban teaching hospitals (87.0%). Overall in-hospital mortality was 0.1% (n = 225, p = 0.582). Minor APR-DRG risk of mortality increased from 43.5% to 55.5%, while all others decreased (p < 0.001). Age-adjusted LAAO rates rose from 34.19 to 379.87 per 100,000 population (p-trend < 0.01). Significant differences in utilization across racial groups persisted throughout the study period. ConclusionsPercutaneous LAAO utilization expanded rapidly with exceptionally low inpatient mortality. Persistent gaps in age-adjusted rates highlight key racial, sex, and geographic disparities in structural heart care. Condensed AbstractUsing the 2016-2022 National Inpatient Sample, this study evaluated temporal trends and demographic adoption patterns of percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO). Among 190,020 weighted procedures, annual volume increased from 4,875 to 60,445. In-hospital mortality was exceptionally low (0.1%). Age-adjusted procedural rates rose from 34.19 to 379.87 per 100,000 population. However, significant disparities persisted, characterized by heavy centralization in urban teaching hospitals (87.0%) and disproportionately lower absolute age-adjusted utilization among female, Black, Hispanic, and Asian/Pacific Islander patients compared to male and White cohorts. Targeted initiatives are needed to ensure equitable access to structural heart interventions.

papers.title: Machine Learning-based Prediction of Pacing-Induced Cardiomyopathy in Patients with Atrioventricular Block Underlying Heart Failure with Mildly Reduced or Preserved Ejection Fraction
papers.abstract: BackgroundPacing-induced cardiomyopathy (PICM) is a major complication of chronic right ventricular pacing and develops in up to 25% of patients. Reliable prediction of PICM may facilitate individualized pacing strategy selection; however, currently available approaches demonstrate limited discriminative performance. This study aimed to develop and validate machine learning (ML) models for predicting PICM in patients with atrioventricular block (AVB) underlying heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction. MethodsIn this multicenter prospective study derived from the RISK-PICM registry (January 2002 to January 2026), 125 patients with AVB who underwent pacemaker implantation were analyzed. PICM was defined as a [≥]10% reduction in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) resulting in an LVEF <50%. Four ML algorithms, including logistic regression, support vector machine, random forest, and XGBoost, were trained using stratified 4-fold cross-validation with hyperparameter optimization and model discrimination was evaluated. ResultsPICM developed in 41 patients (32.8%) during a median follow-up of 4.8 years. Male sex, pre-implant minimum QTc interval, and post-implant maximum QRS duration were significantly associated with PICM in univariable Cox regression. XGBoost achieved the highest discriminative performance (AUROC 0.831; sensitivity 0.805; specificity 0.845). Feature importance analysis identified baseline LVEF and post-implant maximum QRS duration as the most influential features. Model-derived risk stratification significantly differentiated high-risk and low-risk groups on Kaplan-Meier analysis (P < 0.001). ConclusionsML-based models, particularly XGBoost, demonstrated clinically meaningful performance for PICM and may support individualized pacing strategy selection in patients with AVB and underlying heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction. Clinical PerspectiveO_ST_ABSWhat Is NewC_ST_ABSO_LIIn pacing-dependent AVB patients with HFmrEF or HFpEF, ensemble ML (XGBoost) predicted PICM with an AUROC of 0.831. C_LIO_LIModel-derived risk stratification separated PICM-free survival (log-rank P<0.001). C_LI What Are the Clinical ImplicationsO_LIAn ML model combining baseline LVEF, paced QRS duration, and the full parameter set may guide individualized choice between right ventricular and conduction system pacing in AVB patients with HFmrEF or HFpEF. C_LIO_LIUsing paced QRS duration combined with baseline LVEF during temporary pacing in AVB patients with HFmrEF or HFpEF, this risk estimate could inform pacing-strategy selection before permanent implantation, enabling pre-emptive use of conduction system pacing in high-risk patients. C_LI

papers.title: Personalised normative cardiac phenotyping reveals clinically relevant heterogeneity in cardiac shape and outcome risk
papers.abstract: Standard cardiac biomarkers such as ejection fraction, ventricular volumes, and strain compress complex three-dimensional heart dynamics into a small set of predefined measurements, leaving clinically important heterogeneity unrecognised. Here we propose a personalised normative cardiac frame-work in which each individual is compared to a digital twin representing expected healthy cardiac function given their age, sex, and body habitus. We show that structured patterns of deviation from these normative twins, discovered through systematic exploration of a generative cardiac dynamics space, constitute novel dynamic phenotypes that are not captured by conventional biomarkers. Applied independently to two UK Biobank cardiac cohorts with distinct shape representation, a 128-dimensional four-chamber statistical shape descriptor (HeartSSM, n = 52,365) and a 64-dimensional deep generative latent space from a conditional variational mesh autoencoder (MeshHeart cVAE, n = up to 39,376), we identify reproducible, continuous deviation-from-normative-twin scores (three discrete deviation phenotypes in the HeartSSM cohort) that improve cardiovascular risk stratification beyond ejection fraction, ventricular volumes, myocardial mass, and strain. The strongest effect was seen for incident atrial fibrillation among individuals with preserved ejection fraction ([≥]50%): incremental C-index {Delta}C = +0.068 (5-fold cross-validated {Delta}C = +0.063; likelihood-ratio P = 3.3 x 10-8), with a separate, smaller effect for incident stroke in the same preserved-EF subgroup in the independent MeshHeart cVAE representation (which showed no signal for atrial fibrillation) ({Delta}C = +0.024, P = 2.6 x 10-4). Both effects were checked against placebo controls in which the deviation scores were replaced by Gaussian noise. To test whether the normative twin generalises beyond UK Biobanks specific scanning and processing pipeline, we applied the MeshHeart cVAE normative twin, unmodified, to an independent external cohort of healthy volunteers imaged at a different hospital (Gen-Scan/Hammersmith, n = 315): deviation scores in this cohort were of comparable magnitude to the UK Biobank healthy reference (ratio of means = 1.09; Mann-Whitney P = 1.4 x 10-5), indicating that the normative twin captures cross-site-transferable structure rather than a scanner- or pipeline-specific artefact. Our findings suggest that cardiac phenotyping can move beyond predefined measurements toward data-driven dynamic phenotypes that better capture the heterogeneity underlying cardiovascular disease risk, even among individuals whose ejection fraction appears normal.

papers.title: Serial measurements of Growth Differentiation Factor-15 in patients with Non-ST-Elevation Acute Coronary Syndrome and recurrent ischemic events
papers.abstract: BackgroundGrowth differentiation factor 15 (GDF-15) has emerged as a prognostic biomarker in patients with non-ST-segment-elevation acute coronary syndrome (NSTE-ACS). Our study evaluated the temporal evolution of GDF-15 in the acute phase and its association with recurrent ischemic events. MethodsSerum samples were collected from patients with NSTE-ACS at admission and at 1 and 3 hours after admission. GDF-15 levels, along with other prognostic biomarkers, NT-proBNP and hs-cTnT, were measured. Spearmans rank-correlation coefficients and linear regression models were used to identify the variables associated with GDF-15 levels at admission and with their temporal changes. Associations between GDF-15 and clinical outcomes were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models. To assess incremental prognostic value, the areas under the curve (AUC) were calculated for each model. ResultsGDF-15 levels showed a slight increasing trend within 3 hours of admission. The 1-hour change in GDF-15 was correlated with hs-cTnT changes. Increased 1-hour GDF-15 levels, compared with the admission levels, were associated with a higher risk of recurrent ischemic events during the 1-year follow-up (1.9% vs. 17.5%, P =0.019) and were an independent predictor after adjusting for established clinical variables and biomarkers (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.71 [1.28 to 228.75], P =0.03). Furthermore, serial measurements of GDF-15 provided additional prognostic information beyond traditional risk factors. ConclusionsSerial measurements of GDF-15 of NSTE-ACS patients provided independent and incremental prognostic value for predicting recurrent ischemic events. These findings support the potential utility of GDF-15 as a dynamic biomarker for early risk stratification in the acute management of NSTE-ACS.

papers.title: Age-, sex-, and ethnicity-stratified CMR strain reference ranges and centile-based categories from the Healthy Hearts Consortium
papers.abstract: BackgroundThis study presents reference ranges for cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR)-derived myocardial strain from the Healthy Hearts Consortium, while evaluating variations by demographic characteristics (age, sex, and ethnicity) and technical factors (scanner vendor, magnetic field strength). We derived reference ranges and centile-based categories for ventricular, atrial, and rapid strain parameters. The prognostic relevance of these categories was assessed by examining their associations with incident cardiovascular events. MethodsThe dataset included 9,088 CMR studies. Automated image analysis pipelines were established using suiteHEART (NeoSoft Inc.) and cvi42 (Circle Cardiovascular Imaging). A three-step quality control framework was applied including exclusion of incomplete data, visual assessment of image and segmentation quality, and statistical outlier removal. Ventricular strain and strain rate were measured using both software solutions. Additional cvi42-derived metrics included velocity and displacement, annular plane systolic excursion metrics, and rapid strain parameters. Age- and sex-specific reference ranges were generated using lambda-mu-sigma (LMS) modeling with penalized splines. Reference ranges were defined as values between the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles. For lower-tail classification, values below the 2.5th percentile were considered mildly out-of-range and values below the 0.5th percentile at least moderately out-of-range. Differences across scanner vendors (Siemens, Philips, GE) and magnetic field strengths (1.5 T vs. 3 T) were evaluated using adjusted linear models. The prognostic relevance of selected cvi42-derived categories was evaluated in approximately 45,000 UK Biobank participants using Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, and body mass index. ResultsAfter quality control, 8,975 CMR examinations (cvi42) and 8,992 (suiteHEART) were available for analysis; these represent software-specific analytic cohorts. Most exclusions occurred during visual quality control. Women had higher absolute ventricular and atrial strain values than men across all age groups. Left ventricular (LV) longitudinal strain and strain rate were slightly lower in older ages, whereas circumferential and radial parameters remained largely stable. Left atrial strain was also lower in older age groups, while right atrial strain did not vary by age. Annular plane systolic excursion and rapid strain metrics showed similar sex-specific patterns, with modestly lower atrial and displacement values in older groups. Ethnicity-related differences were modest, heterogeneous, and substantially smaller in magnitude than age- and sex-related differences. Technical effects were parameter specific. While LV longitudinal and circumferential strains were largely unaffected, radial strain was higher at 3 T and showed vendor-related differences. LMS-derived reference ranges and centile thresholds were applied both across all ethnicities and within ethnicity-specific analyses, and are presented stratified by age and sex. In the prognostic analysis, centile categories were most consistently associated with incident heart failure. LV longitudinal, circumferential, and radial strain below the 0.5th centile were associated with significantly increased risk of incident heart failure (HRs: 9.9 to 12.4, 95% CIs 7.00-13.90 to 8.49-18.06). ConclusionThis study provides age- and sex-specific reference ranges and centile-based categories for CMR-derived strain parameters in a large reference population. Age and sex represent the primary determinants of myocardial deformation, whereas scanner-related effects are parameter-specific. Values in the lower extremes of the healthy reference distribution, particularly for LV strain, are associated with increased risk of incident heart failure. These findings enable standardized, centile-based classification of myocardial strain, facilitating consistent interpretation and improving risk stratification in research and clinical practice.

papers.title: Atrial fibrillation begets atrial fibrillation - serum-driven amplification of atrial electrical instability
papers.abstract: RationaleAtrial fibrillation (AF) is sustained by electrical triggers and atrial substrate, but whether AF itself generates circulating factors that acutely reinforce arrhythmogenesis is unknown. ObjectiveTo determine whether rhythm-dependent serum bioactivity directly destabilizes atrial electrophysiology and to identify associated cellular mechanisms and circulating mediators. Methods and ResultsCardiac samples were obtained from patients with persistent atrial fibrillation (AF) during AF and after restoration of sinus rhythm (SR) using electrical cardioversion. In isolated Langendorff-perfused mouse hearts, AF serum increased the duration, frequency, and cumulative burden of spontaneous atrial depolarizations compared with paired control perfusate. In human induced pluripotent stem cell derived atrial cardiomyocytes, AF patient serum decreased Ca{superscript 2}-transient amplitudes without significant effect on kinetics or Ca{superscript 2} spark activity. Moreover, AF serum reduced peak sodium current without materially altering voltage-dependent gating or paced action-potential properties. Data-independent acquisition proteomics identified rhythm-associated changes in extracellular-matrix, proteolytic, inflammatory, and signaling proteins, including MMP9, Ccathepsin G, and 14-3-3 family members. Targeted pathway perturbation differentially modified serum-induced Ca{superscript 2} phenotypes, indicating context-dependent, multifactorial bioactivity. Serum-induced Ca{superscript 2} responses were not associated with indices of atrial disease severity, including low-voltage substrate burden and left atrial pressure. ConclusionsPersistent AF is accompanied by rhythm-dependent circulating bioactivity that acutely promotes atrial electrical instability and Ca{superscript 2}-dependent trigger formation. These findings extend the concept that "AF begets AF" beyond tissue-intrinsic remodeling and identify a potentially reversible serum-mediated feed-forward mechanism linking rhythm status and circulating proteomic signals in an atrial substrate severity independent fashion.

papers.title: Uneven Recovery of Exercise Training in US Adults With Cardiovascular Risk Factors or Disease Following the COVID 19 Pandemic
papers.abstract: IntroductionThe COVID-19 pandemic led to significant disruptions in cardiovascular care and reductions in physical activity, but little is known about how exercise patterns changed after this period. This study assessed changes in weekly aerobic and strength training activity between 2020 and 2022 amongst adults aged 18 years or older who reported one or more cardiovascular diseases or risk factors. MethodsThis study used National Health Interview Survey data from 2020 and 2022. Adjusted differences for moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) were calculated using a linear regression model and for strength sessions using a Poisson regression, adjusting for sex and age. Changes in these outcomes were then stratified by age and sex subgroups. ResultsThe weighted study population included 182,783,008 (standard error, {+/-}3,334,337) adults in 2020 and 185,388,060 (SE, {+/-}3,285,161) adults in 2022. Between 2020 and 2022, the overall weekly MVPA increased from 244.2 (SE, {+/-}4.5) minutes to 266.3 (SE, {+/-}5.7) minutes (adjusted difference, +22.1 [SE, {+/-}6.92] minutes). There were no statistically significant changes in the number of strength session per week overall or among sex and age subgroups. Across sex and age subgroups, increases in weekly MVPA were entirely concentrated among males and younger adults. ConclusionThe recovery from pandemic era reductions in aerobic and strength exercise training was uneven amongst demographic subgroups, which aligns with concurrent persistent disruptions in cardiovascular care.

papers.title: Efficacy of Disease-Modifying Treatments in Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Five Phase III Randomized Controlled Trials
papers.abstract: BackgroundSeveral disease-modifying agents for transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) have been investigated, but differences in trial design and background stabilizer use complicate interpretation of their efficacy. This meta-analysis assessed their efficacy overall and by background stabilizer use. MethodsPubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched through September 2026 for phase III randomized, placebo-controlled trials of disease-modifying therapy in ATTR-CM. Primary endpoints were all-cause mortality, 6-minute walk distance (6MWD), Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-Overall Summary (KCCQ-OS) score, and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), pooled with a random-effects model. Treatment effects were compared between the monotherapy and baseline stabilizer strata using a mixed-effects model. ResultsFive trials (ATTR-ACT, APOLLO-B, ATTRibute-CM, HELIOS-B, CARDIO-TTRansform; N=3497) were included. Disease-modifying therapy reduced all-cause mortality (risk ratio, 0.76; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.66-0.87; I2=0%) and improved 6MWD (pooled standardized mean difference [SMD], 0.43; 95% CI, 0.20-0.67), KCCQ-OS score (SMD, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.19-0.55), and NT-proBNP (SMD, - 0.53; 95% CI, -0.89 to -0.18). The mortality benefit was similar whether therapy was given alone or added to a background stabilizer (pooled risk ratio, 0.77 vs. 0.71; P for interaction = 0.59), but treatment effects on 6MWD (pooled SMD, 0.49 vs. 0.14), KCCQ-OS score (0.44 vs. 0.07), and NT-proBNP (-0.65 vs. -0.13) were smaller among patients receiving a background stabilizer (P for interaction = 0.012, <0.001, and 0.029, respectively). ConclusionDisease-modifying treatments reduced all-cause mortality and favored functional capacity, health status, and NT-proBNP outcomes in patients with ATTR-CM. Exploratory subgroup analyses showed smaller treatment effects on 6MWD, KCCQ-OS score, and NT-proBNP among patients receiving a background stabilizer, with no statistically significant difference in the mortality effect according to baseline stabilizer use. What Is New?O_LIThis meta-analysis of all five phase III randomized controlled trials of disease-modifying therapy in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (3497 analyzed participants) found a lower risk of all-cause mortality (risk ratio, 0.76; 95% CI, 0.66-0.87) and more favorable 6-minute walk distance, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-Overall Summary score, and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP). C_LIO_LIIn subgroup analyses, the mortality effect was similar with and without a background transthyretin stabilizer at randomization, whereas effects on functional capacity, health status, and NT-proBNP were smaller among patients receiving a background stabilizer. C_LI What Are the Clinical Implications?O_LIAmong patients already receiving a transthyretin stabilizer, adding a second agent was associated with a mortality reduction similar to that seen without background therapy but with smaller incremental gains in functional and biomarker outcomes; because these findings rest on aggregate trial data and subgroup comparisons, they should be interpreted cautiously. C_LI

papers.title: Ascending Aortic Calcium Identifies Patients at Risk Despite Normal Myocardial Flow, Perfusion and Coronary Calcium: A 13-Site Cohort Study
papers.abstract: BackgroundPatients with normal perfusion, normal myocardial flow reserve (MFR) and no coronary artery calcium (CAC) on myocardial perfusion imaging are considered low risk. Yet, adverse events still occur and no routinely reported imaging marker stratifies residual risk. This study aims to determine whether fully automated ascending aortic calcification (AAC) from the attenuation correction CT stratifies risk in these patients. MethodsIn the multicenter REFINE-PET registry, AAC was quantified from non-contrast CT using deep learning aortic segmentation and Agatston scoring. Triple-normal was defined as stress total perfusion deficit (TPD) 2 and CAC 0. The primary endpoint was cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction or heart failure admission, with heart failure admission as key secondary endpoint. Cox models were adjusted for clinical confounders. ResultsOf 21,923 patients, 3,580 (16.3%) were triple-normal, of whom 1,322 (36.9%) had AAC (median Agatston 65, IQR 22-212). Agreement with three blinded readers was good to excellent (Intraclass correlation coefficient 0.87-0.90). Over a median follow-up of 52 months (IQR 26-69), 194 primary events occurred. Per standard deviation, AAC was independently associated with the primary endpoint (adjusted HR 1.24, 95% CI 1.09-1.40; p<0.001), heart failure admission (adjusted HR 1.30, 95% CI 1.10-1.55; p=0.003) and all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 1.17, 95% CI 1.04-1.32; p=0.009). AAC improved model fit beyond clinical factors, MFR and TPD (p[≤]0.009), with modest gains in discrimination ({Delta}C 0.007-0.009). ConclusionsIn patients with normal PET readouts, automated AAC was independently associated with adverse outcomes, most strongly heart failure admission, beyond clinical risk factors, perfusion and flow. Clinical PerspectiveO_ST_ABSWhat Is New?C_ST_ABSO_LIIn 3,580 patients with normal perfusion, normal myocardial flow reserve and no coronary artery calcium on PET, more than one in three had ascending aortic calcification on the attenuation correction CT. C_LIO_LIAscending aortic calcification was independently associated with cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction or heart failure admission (adjusted hazard ratio per SD 1.24, 95% CI 1.09-1.40), most strongly with heart failure admission. C_LIO_LIA fast, fully automated method scored ascending aortic calcification with agreement to expert readers similar to agreement between readers. C_LI What Are the Clinical Implications?O_LIA normal perfusion PET with normal flow and no coronary calcium does not mean uniformly low risk when the ascending aorta is calcified. C_LIO_LIBecause ascending aortic calcification is scored automatically from the CT acquired with every perfusion PET, it could be reported routinely without additional scanning, cost or radiation. C_LIO_LIPatients presumed low risk who have ascending aortic calcification may warrant heart failure-oriented prevention, such as natriuretic peptide screening, pending prospective validation. C_LI

papers.title: Population-scale trends and variations in human aortic biomechanics
papers.abstract: The biomechanical properties of the human aorta play a key role in cardiovascular function and disease, yet their population-wide trends and variations remain largely unknown. To fill this crucial gap, we quantified variations in aortic size, stiffness and stresses across 57,434 individuals from the UK Biobank using two-dimensional cine MR imaging and a combined deep-learning, probabilistic and biomechanical modelling framework. Aortic diameter and distensibility (inverse of stiffness) were calculated for the ascending and descending aorta, and their conditional distributions were characterised as a function of age, sex, body size and blood pressure. These observations were integrated with ex-vivo tissue mechanics to infer stress distributions across the aortic wall and the associated uncertainty. Our analysis revealed several new relationships. Larger aortas were found to be stiffer, and greater body size (height and/or weight) was associated with larger aortas with no change in stiffness. Aortic distensibility was negatively associated with systolic, but not diastolic, blood pressure. Apparent sex differences in aortic size were substantially reduced after accounting for body size. Importantly, the maximum stress was found to depend not only on aortic size, as previously thought, but also on distensibility, with lower distensibility associated with higher stresses. The results provide first-of-their-kind population-scale reference distributions for human aortic stiffness, which will improve the personalisation of computational models and digital twins. The correlation between stress and distensibility strongly supports progressing beyond the current diameter-based criteria (based on the law of Laplace) and for the inclusion of stiffness in the clinical risk assessment of aortic diseases. Overall, this study forms the foundation for personalised quantitative medicine and biomechanically informed risk stratification of aortic aneurysms and dissections.

papers.title: 30-Day Heart Failure Readmission and Post-Discharge Healthcare Use Among Older Australians: A Linked-Data Mixed-Methods Study
papers.abstract: BackgroundHeart failure (HF) is a major public health challenge in ageing populations and a leading cause of unplanned hospital readmissions. Biological, social, and economic factors contribute to recurrent hospitalisation, but gaps remain in understanding how these factors interact and patterns of healthcare use following hospitalisation. MethodsWe conducted an explanatory sequential mixed-methods study of patients aged [≥]60 years with an HF hospital admission between 2016 and 2020 who completed the Sax Institutes 45 and Up Study baseline questionnaire. Data were linked to Admitted Patient Data Collection, Medicare Benefits Schedule, and Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme data. HF readmission within 30 days of the index admission was the outcome. Cox proportional hazards models estimated crude and adjusted hazard ratios (HRs and adjHRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Kaplan-Meier curves and log-rank tests compared survival between groups. Time-series plots mapped healthcare interactions over 1 year following the index admission. ResultsAmong 4,252 patients with HF, 409 were readmitted within 30 days. Significant predictors included age [≥]80 years (adjHR, 1.30; 95%CI, 1.01-1.67), 1 chronic condition (adjHR, 2.49; 95%CI, 1.41-4.40), [≥]2 chronic conditions (adjHR, 1.75; 95%CI, 1.04-2.95), and alcohol consumption above national guidelines (adjHR, 1.45; 95%CI, 1.06-1.98). Time-series analysis indicated that participants with readmission had more frequent out-of-hospital health service contact following their initial HF admission than those without readmission. ConclusionsOlder age, chronic conditions, and high alcohol intake increased 30-day HF readmission risk. Differences in healthcare use after admission highlight opportunities for targeted and coordinated post-discharge care.
